Chapter 5 of 5
05

Reality check
and outlook

What got in the way, and what we learned.

Reality check: Sommerville’s risk classes

4 things that got in the way

Each one forced a decision about how we work.

01

CI credits ran outProject risk

Release jobs stopped. We switched to manual reviews and local checks.

02

Parallel agents collidedProject risk

Two agents built on the same database version. Now each agent gets its own files, so they can’t overlap.

03

Emulators hid bugsProduct risk

With “Remove animations” on, home tiles vanished on a real phone. All emulator tests were green.

04

Rules written, not followedProject risk

The spec said American spelling. The briefs didn’t. The app was built in British. Now every rule goes into every brief.

Reality check: Scope, time and cost are coupled

Writing code got fast - delivering it didn’t

Feature example 1 · Writing code: voice input, 24 Oct

4 tickets, 4 agents at the same time.

Each agent had its own files, so they never got in each other’s way.
One after another, it would have taken about 30 minutes.
8:48
minutes for all 4, instead of about 30
Feature example 2 · Delivering it: UX work, 25–27 Oct

12 tickets planned for 7 agents.

The agents hit their usage limit 3 times and had to stop.
Meanwhile the team kept changing the app, so agents spent time catching up instead of building.

Fixed time and budget meant scope took the hit.

5 / 12
planned tickets finished and merged after 2 days
Outlook: testing with users next

4 phases, 1 exit test each

Business model

Free for users. Partner shops pay commission on sales via Shopping Hub.

Today
Phase 1 · released 31 Oct

MVP

First increment on the team's own phones, as an APK.

Exit when

Every Must-have passes its acceptance test on a real phone

Phase 2 · now

Alpha

Test internally; improve usability and recommendations.

Exit when

2 weeks of daily team use; outfit quality holds at the current level

Phase 3 · next

Beta

A limited group of real users; measure usefulness.

Exit when

10 outside testers for 2 weeks; most testers use suggestions regularly

Phase 4

Launch and growth

Reliability, privacy requirements and scale.

Exit when

Weekly use of the daily outfit holds for a month

Outlook: lessons learned

What we take with us

AI made building cheap. Deciding, testing and scoping still needed people.

1

Decide before you build

Put every rule in every brief. No surprises in review.

2

Verify on real devices

Real tests on real phones. Green checks can lie.

3

Know your free-tier limits

Free tiers run out. Know the limits before you start.

4

Launching needs human experts

AI ships the prototype. Humans ship the product.

Backup · Agent team

The best model plans. Cheaper ones write the code.

The set-up of one session. Every team member merges their own pull requests once checks are green.

Owner · human

Decides

Sets goals, approves plans and mock-ups, says “merge #N”, deploys the proxy, keeps every secret.

Orchestrator · Opus 5.5

Plans and reviews

Splits work into issues, writes one brief per issue, reviews every diff, resolves conflicts.

Feature agents · Sonnet 5.5

Build

One issue each, in its own worktree: code, tests, docs and a pull request.

Small tasks · Haiku 5.5

Tidy up

Small, clearly bounded changes: remove dead code, re-wire a button.

Backup · Rules and governance

Autonomy is agreed rules, not trust alone.

Agent mode · human in the loop
  • Plan first; UI starts with an ASCII mock-up
  • Questions come as options with a recommendation
  • One agent, one issue, one worktree
  • A precise brief that says “do not merge”
  • Nothing lives only in the chat
Night mode · human above the loop
  • First run on 22 Oct, before our busiest day
  • Keep building the agreed plan
  • Owner questions wait on a morning list
  • Merge only after review and green CI
  • Deploys, secrets and decisions stay human
Definition of Done
  • Acceptance checked by the owner
  • Unit tests, all green
  • Tried on an emulator or a phone
  • Texts in all 21 app languages
  • New findings written into docs/
Backup · AI proxy as broker

One door, nine routes, hard limits.

A Cloudflare Worker on the free plan. The app holds no secret; Steve S. deploys it, agents never do.

RoutesRecognise items, rank outfits, update the style file, classify styles, and five for products from eBay
Limits10 requests a minute and 200 a day per install, 450 a day in total, below the free quota
AccessAn anonymous install token instead of accounts; a single install can be blocked (ADR-0015)
ModelGemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, pinned; answers forced into a JSON schema with fixed values
KeysGemini and eBay keys only as Worker secrets, never in the repository

Agents edit the same fileProjectMediumMediumOccurred: database version 4Plan work by file ownership2 tickets share a file → run one after the other

Emulator hides device bugsProductMediumHighOccurred: #346, Galaxy A54 (fixed in #363)Test on a real phoneDevice-only bug → add a real-phone check to the Definition of Done (it allows an emulator today)
Parallel agents share one laptopProjectHighMediumOccurred: 22 Oct, emulator crashed mid-testDevice tests between agent wavesFree memory low → run one wave at a time

Backup · Inspect before you test

Privacy was decided before it was built

Written down in the privacy concept and the ADRs, then checked in review.

Decisions we made
Local first

The closet lives on the phone. No account is needed.

Faces blurred on the phone

ADR-0013: ML Kit finds faces on the phone. Nothing is sent to find them.

You decide

“Send this photo?” appears before every upload.

Free AI tier

ADR-0003: test photos only in development.

Backup · Verification vs. validation

Verified, not yet validated.

Tests show we built it right. Only real users show we built the right thing.

Users

No real users yet

The personas are hypotheses from desk research.

Shopping

Not tested with shoppers

The Shopping Hub is in the app, but key features are still in development.

Photos

Only our own photos

Recognition was checked on the team's test photos, not on users' closets.
